newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark rallies in Europe, Buba gives blessing.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark rallies in Europe, Buba gives blessing.

text.p: The dollar motored higher above 1.70 marks in Europe on Wednesday as Bundesbank officials signalled satisfaction with current levels and speculation was rekindled about a rise in U.S. interest rates next week.

Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said in Vienna "It seems that a dollar rate at around 1.70 marks conforms with the real data." His Bundesbank colleague Klaus-Dieter Kuebacher said later in Warsaw he also believed dollar/mark levels were good.
The dollar/mark performance stood in marked constrast to a subdued dollar/yen, which traders now think will be capped at 120 by official protestations or even central bank sales.
The differing fortunes of the mark and yen precipitated another sharp slide in the mark/yen cross to its lowest level since May 1996 at 69.45. Charts say there is scope now to 69.05.
"The mark/yen rate really is the 'big sell' when you compare relative policy trends in Europe and Japan," said Michael Burke, economist at Citibank.
"The Japanese made it abundantly clear last week where they want dollar/yen to go and the Bundesbank comments today amount to a verbal floor under 1.70."
At 1100 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7065/70 marks, up one pfennig from Tuesday's close in Europe at 1.6964/69.
"Welteke is certainly giving the impression the weakness of the mark is not a problem at these levels," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
Against the yen, the dollar was trading at 118.69/79 compared with 118.65/75 late yesterday.
Although the dollar underperformed against the yen, it was supported by renewed talk of a U.S. rate rise next week.

Richmond Federal Reserve chied Alfred Broaddus said the U.S. economy was expanding rapidly and labour markets remained tight. Sources close to the Fed told Reuters there is a good chance of another 25 basis point rise in the Fed funds rate on May 20.

"The market now being torn two ways on next week's Fed meeting - the talking is still tough but the data looks soft," said Brian Hilliard, chief economist at Societe Generale. "At the end of the day, I still think it's a matter of when not if."
A brief rally in dollar/yen above 119 overnight, meantime, was short-lived and met with a wave of dollar sales from funds and exporters in Tokyo, traders said.

Traders said there is a growing belief that both Japanese industry and the authorities are now happy to keep a lid on the dollar at 120 following last week's successful verbal intervention to weaken it from close to 4-1/2-year highs.

The dollar/yen got a brief fillip in Tokyo from news of a 17 percent year-on-year drop in Japan's March current account surplus and rumours, later denied, that a major Japanese bank suffered large foreign exchange losses at overseas operations.
Analysts said, however, the current account picture in the second quarter is now of more interest. Forecasts suggest the surplus has widened again since March.
Sterling/mark gained up to three pfennigs, aided by a robust UK unemployment report for April which showed the labour market tightening further but with an easing of wage and earnings pressures.

The UK jobless total fell a bigger-than-expected 59,400 during the month and the unemployment rate fell to 5.9 percent from 6.1 percent in March. Average earnings were unchanged at 4.5 percent in March.
The pound was capped later, however, as UK foreign secretary Robin Cook told Le Monde newspaper he was in favour of joining European monetary union longer term if it proved a success.
Elsewhere, some traders said the dollar got a lift from sharp slides in the Thai baht and the Czech crown while growing official optimism about a punctual EMU start hurt on the mark.
--Mike Dolan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6762
